title: Set 270

sentences.ko: 나 도자기 배우기 시작했다고 했던 거 기억나? 그거 있잖아, 한 네 번 정도 갔는데, 일 때문에 한 번 빠지고 나서는 그냥 다시 안 갔어. 수강료도 이미 전부 내 놨었거든, 그래서 좀 민망해.
sentences.text: Remember when I said I was getting into pottery? Yeah, I went to like four classes, and then I missed one because of work, and after that I just never went back. I'd already paid for the whole thing, too, so that's kind of embarrassing.

alts.text: You know the pottery thing I told you about? I made it to like four classes, missed one for work, and just never went back after that. And I'd already paid for the whole thing, so yeah, kinda embarrassing.

Do you recall when I mentioned that I was taking up pottery? I attended about four classes, then missed one because of work, and after that I simply never returned. I had already paid for the entire course as well, so it is rather embarrassing.

sentences.note: **getting into** 는 어떤 취미에 재미를 붙이기 시작하다라는 뜻입니다. **never went back** 은 그 뒤로 다시는 안 갔다는 말이고, 캐주얼의 **made it to** 는 어떻게든 가긴 갔다는 느낌입니다.

sentences.ko: 자리 찾기 전에 음료부터 받은 게 큰 실수였어, 남은 자리가 하나도 없었거든. 그래서 결국 누가 드디어 일어나서 나갈 때까지 컵 들고 창가에 서 있었어.
sentences.text: We got our drinks before we looked for a table, which was a big mistake, because there wasn't a single seat left. So we ended up standing by the window holding our cups until somebody finally got up and left.

alts.text: Big mistake. We grabbed our drinks before finding a table, and there wasn't one seat left. So we just stood by the window holding our cups till somebody finally got up and left.

We purchased our drinks before looking for a table, which was a serious mistake, because there was not a single seat available. As a result, we stood by the window holding our cups until someone finally got up and left.

sentences.note: **ended up** 은 의도와 달리 결국 ~하게 됐다는 뜻입니다. **there wasn't a single seat left** 는 자리가 단 하나도 안 남았다고 강조하는 말입니다.

sentences.ko: 늦어서 미안해! 옆집 사람 차가 내 차를 막고 있어서, 그 집에 가서 문 두드리고 그분이 내려와서 차 빼 줄 때까지 기다려야 했어.
sentences.text: Sorry I'm late! My neighbor's car was blocking mine, so I had to go knock on her door and then wait for her to come down and move it.

alts.text: Ugh, sorry I'm late! My neighbor had my car blocked in, so I had to go knock on her door and wait till she came down to move it.
I apologize for being late. My neighbor's car was blocking mine, so I had to knock on her door and then wait for her to come down and move it.

sentences.note: **blocking** 은 길이나 차를 막고 있다는 뜻입니다. 캐주얼의 **had my car blocked in** 은 내 차가 갇혀서 못 나가게 막혔다는 표현입니다.

sentences.ko: 3월에 월세가 200달러 오르거든, 그래서 좀 더 외곽에 있는 집들을 알아보고 있어. 근데 이사 가면 차로 출근해야 되는데, 그 돈 아끼자고 매일 차에서 한 시간씩 더 보내는 게 맞나 싶어.
sentences.text: My rent's going up two hundred dollars in March, so I've been looking at places farther out. But if I move, I'd have to drive to work, and I'm not sure the money I'd save is worth spending an extra hour in the car every day.

alts.text: They're bumping my rent up two hundred bucks in March, so I've been checking out places farther out. But if I move I'd have to drive to work, and I dunno if what I'd save is worth an extra hour in the car every day.

My rent will increase by two hundred dollars in March, so I have been looking at places farther out. However, if I move, I would need to drive to work, and I am not certain that the money I would save is worth spending an additional hour in the car each day.

sentences.note: **farther out** 은 도심에서 더 떨어진 곳을 말합니다. **worth spending** 은 ~하는 데 쓸 만한 가치가 있다는 뜻이고, 캐주얼의 **bumping** 은 값을 올린다는 구어입니다.

sentences.ko: 아니야 아빠, 돈 필요 없어, 나 괜찮아. 이번 달에 차 좀 고칠 데가 있어서 살짝 빠듯한 것뿐이지, 내가 감당 못 할 정도는 아니야. 진짜로, 아무것도 보내지 마.
sentences.text: No, Dad, I don't need any money, I'm fine. I just had to get some stuff fixed on my car this month, so things are a little tight, but it's nothing I can't handle. Seriously, don't send anything.

alts.text: I'm good, Dad, really, I don't need money. Just had to get some car stuff fixed this month, so it's a little tight, but I've got it covered. Seriously, don't send anything.

No, Dad, I do not need any money. I am fine. I simply had to have some repairs done on my car this month, so things are somewhat tight, but it is nothing I cannot manage. Truly, please do not send anything.

sentences.note: **things are a little tight** 는 돈 사정이 좀 빠듯하다는 뜻입니다. **nothing I can't handle** 은 내가 감당 못 할 일은 아니다, 충분히 괜찮다는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: 부모님 안부 전화에서 잘 지낸다고 둘러대기

reviewed: 1번 한국어: 스스로 던진 질문에 '응,' 으로 답하는 것이 한국어로는 어색해서 '그거 있잖아,' 로 바꿈
2번 casual: 'Big mistake, we grabbed...' 가 쉼표로 두 문장을 붙인 꼴이라 마침표로 나누고 'and' 로 이음
4번 casual: 'bumping my rent two hundred bucks' 는 'bumping my rent up' 이 더 자연스러워 up 을 넣음
4번 한국어: '아끼는 돈이 ... 버릴 만큼 가치가 있는지' 가 번역투라 '그 돈 아끼자고 ... 보내는 게 맞나 싶어' 로 고침
4번 formal: 'places located farther out' 의 located 가 글말 같아 뺌
5번 formal: 아빠에게 하는 말에서 'Father' 는 말투가 아니라 관계까지 바꿔 버려 'Dad' 로 되돌림
5번 casual: 'I got it' 만으로는 무엇을 감당한다는 건지 흐려서 'I've got it covered' 로 고침
